direction: Toward the literature: verified scoped effects, opposing endpoints, SD definitions and unresolved extractions; no certification changes.

sources.limits: Direct evidence for this rice cultivar, soil and irrigation contrast only. Not a universal irrigation prescription; not evidence for ingredient processing or finished infant formula.

locators: Abstract; Methods: Cooking rice in different volumes of water; Results paragraphs 2–3 and Figure 1.
sources.limits: Direct evidence for the tested grain forms and 12:1 laboratory method. No Cd effect, infant formula effect, baby-cereal manufacturing effect or rice-milk effect is inferred.

Consider site-specific biochar immobilization where Cd-contaminated soil is already established. The maximum 26.25% in the abstract is not a guaranteed effect. Exact year-specific CK/C3 grain means and dispersion require extraction; do not infer commercial efficacy.

locators: Results paragraphs 1–2; Table 1; Methods and 31 January 2020 correction.
sources.limits: Use regional evidence to shortlist candidates, then verify the actual supplier and lot. Do not promise a regional reduction percentage or a universally low-contaminant origin; current lots require testing.

locators: Introduction paragraph beginning Milling; cited references 6 and 7.
sources.limits: Evaluate polishing where product requirements allow; test endosperm and bran separately. No milling reduction percentage is presented as verified intervention evidence; contextual research requires appraisal.

locators: Results opening paragraph; Figure 1 caption; Sampling strategy and Discussion.
sources.limits: Evaluate suitable alternative grains in a new recipe and test the finished product. This is product design, not permission to dilute a nonconforming lot. No current legal acceptability or fixed reduction factor is inferred.

locators: Guidance recommendations to manufacturers: selective sourcing and testing rice and rice-derived ingredients.
sources.limits: Use qualified suppliers, incoming iAs testing and finished-food verification to prevent unsuitable material entering the product. A released COA is not a whole-lot guarantee. No current all-jurisdiction legal appraisal is implied.

locators: Get strategies for rice and infant rice cereal; paragraphs on pasta-style cooking and nutrient losses.
sources.limits: Where suitable for the rice and nutritional needs, use excess cooking water and drain it. Reduces residual rice arsenic; no Cd reduction or individual health outcome is established.

locators: Eat a varied and nutritious diet; Get strategies for rice and infant rice cereal.
sources.limits: Avoid relying on rice products as the only grain; use age-appropriate alternatives, retaining adequate nutrition. Diet diversity does not remove contamination from rice already grown or processed.

locators: Final paragraph under Get strategies for rice and infant rice cereal.
sources.limits: Treat rinsing as preparation, not a demonstrated broad heavy-metal remediation step. No laboratory chemical soaking procedure is recommended for consumers.

boundaries: Nonflooded versus Flood, separately by study year; four AWD arms remain distinct and uncompiled.
Repeated mesocosms and outcomes count as one experiment family.
Reported source total As and iAs do not reconcile in some arms; no species fraction computed.
Cooking estimate is source-reported; ± definition unresolved; not combined with percolation results.
Formula has no exact-matrix intervention effect estimate from these sources.
Observational sourcing/formulation contrasts are not assigned treatment-effect percentages.
Guidance and literature context are labelled as such, not independent datasets.
No supported storage, packaging or universal all-metal removal factor established in this selected evidence. These stages retain verification requirements, not invented treatments.
